It's the 90s, I turn 12 and my father tells me I am too old to play video games. He tells me that I will never receive one again as a present and that I am forbidden to buy one with my own money as long as I lived under his roof.

Fast forward about 10 years. My father has forgotten about this and he mentions that one of his coworkers is playing WoW. I see an opportunity, I buy him a copy for Christmas, and I show him how to play it. For the next few years, it's all he can talk about. He rushes home from work to play it and spends virtually his entire weekends playing it. When I visit for birthday parties, it's hard to pull him away from the computer. When he's away from the game for a couple of hours he gets cranky. My parents have to buy a new laptop so that he can play it in the living room when people are over.

It has now been about another ten years. I visited my folks a couple of weeks ago and he showed me his new keep.

Revenge.

No matter how well you plan, some of it is pure luck. TE's are the most unpredictable, and I put in Fleener because my active TE never broke out of the 2-6 point range. Fleener happens to catch 2 TD's that week and get 22 points. Then there's Peyton Manning who managed to get 0 points one week. But as Lejault said, pay attention to who your players are facing. If it's a rivalry game or your good RB is going against a team shutting down RB's each week, take that into consideration. You can't get around back luck like with Peterson, or injuries to your best players, but you can plan ahead based on who your team is facing.

Here's a common sense scenario for someone like me with Foster and Moreno, 1 injury prone RB and another RB out for the season, I obviously needed a RB. The Denver Broncos are a high offense team. RB's always get the ball, unlike WR's. The Broncos are down to their 3rd string RB to start. The best offense in the NFL is putting a player up who is guaranteed to get the ball. I picked up CJ Anderson and immediately started him, who ended up being one of the RB's of the season. When people even questioned whether to start him I though they were nuts. If a great WR is moving from a team with a bad QB to a team with a good QB during the season and you need a WR, there's your pick. TE's will always be hit and miss, pay attention to team makeup. If your mediocre QB is going against the Texans defense, you will probably throw some interceptions or get sacked too many times to get the ball off.
